questions.q: What level of detail does sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states report?
options: Replica-level role, connection state, and aggregated synchronization health
Only the current backup history for each database
Per-transaction commit timestamps
Only the listener's DNS resolution status
questions.explain: This DMV reports role_desc, connected_state_desc, and synchronization_health_desc at the replica level.

questions.q: Why is sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states needed in addition to the replica-level DMV?
options: Because an AG can hold multiple databases, and any individual database could fall behind or lose sync even if the replica overall looks connected
Because it reports information about a completely unrelated feature, backup compression
Because the replica-level DMV doesn't exist in any SQL Server version
Because it replaces the need for the Always On dashboard entirely
questions.explain: Since AGs can contain multiple databases, database-level granularity is needed to catch a single database falling out of sync while the replica connection itself still looks healthy.

questions.q: What does a growing redo_queue_size on a secondary indicate, per this lesson?
options: The secondary is falling behind — log data has been received but not yet replayed
The primary has stopped accepting new writes
The listener has lost its DNS registration
The database has been switched to SIMPLE recovery model
questions.explain: redo_queue_size measures KB of log data received but not yet replayed on the secondary; a growing value is an early sign the secondary can't keep up.

questions.q: What does the SSMS Always On Dashboard provide, per this lesson?
options: A visual, color-coded presentation of the same underlying DMV data — replica roles, sync health, failover readiness, and estimated data loss
A way to automatically script alerting without any DMV queries
A tool that replaces the need for WSFC quorum
A dashboard exclusive to Azure SQL Database, not on-prem SQL Server
questions.explain: The dashboard is a manual, visual tool for eyeballing AG health, built on the same DMV data — but scripted alerting still relies on querying the DMVs directly.

questions.q: A secondary shows CONNECTED at the replica level, but one database on it shows synchronization_state_desc = NOT SYNCHRONIZING. Which DMV surfaced this, and why would the replica-level DMV alone have missed it?
options: sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states surfaced it — the replica-level DMV aggregates health across all databases and can look fine even when one specific database has fallen out of sync
sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states surfaced it, and the replica-level view always catches this
Neither DMV can report database-level synchronization state
This detail can only be found in the SQL Server error log, not any DMV
questions.explain: The database-level DMV, sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states, is what reports per-database synchronization_state_desc — the replica-level view aggregates and could miss a single out-of-sync database.
